test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Kiran has 24 white beads and Resham has 18 black beads. They want to arrange the beads in such a way that each row contains an equal number of beads and each row must contain either only black beads or only white beads. What is the greatest number of beads that can be arranged in a row?
solution:
**GIVEN:**

No. of white beads Kiran has = 24

No. of black beads Resham has = 18

Each row contains equal no. of beads.

Each row contains either only white or black bead

**CONCEPT USED:**

Highest Common Factor (H. C. F )

**CALCULATION :**

** **24 = 2 × 3 × 4 × 1

18 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 1

We have four possibilities 

⇒ 1 bead in each row

⇒ 2 beads in each row

⇒ 3 beads in each row

⇒ 6 beads in each row 

⇒ In all other cases, rows will get more than one colour of beads.

**⇒ Hence, the greatest number of beads that can be arranged in a row is 6.**
